schema.$comment: JSON Schema describes portable decoded JSON shape. The runtime additionally enforces aggregate UTF-8 byte/value limits and rejects JavaScript-only non-JSON authority such as accessors, proxies, cycles, exotic prototypes, sparse arrays, symbols, non-finite numbers, and negative zero.

commands.description: Repository command evidence settings; configuration never executes commands.

efficiency.description: Static token accounting inputs. B06 defines shape and defaults; G06 owns score formula semantics.

componentWeights.description: Integer percentage weights. Runtime validation additionally requires their sum to equal 100.

gradeThresholds.description: Inclusive grade floors. Runtime validation additionally requires A > B > C > D.

limits.description: Hard upper bounds consumed by later discovery, parsing, import, and diagnostic stages.

security.description: Conservative policy inputs for later rules. These flags never grant filesystem or network capability.

standards.description: Local standards selection. Network access remains an explicit standards-command concern.

schema.description: Closed schema for .agent-context-lint.yml after safe YAML decoding. Unknown structural keys are rejected.

ignore.description: Ordered, unique, root-relative POSIX glob patterns. Backslashes and absolute patterns are rejected.

profiles.description: Per-client and per-surface enablement. Omitted profiles and surfaces are enabled.

rules.description: Rule severity overrides and the version-1 maxTokens option. Rule IDs must use ACL followed by three digits.

schema.title: Agent Context Linter repository configuration v1

entries.description: Invalid YAML/MDC frontmatter
entries.rationale: Malformed frontmatter prevents a client from interpreting declared instruction metadata reliably.

entries.description: Frontmatter field has the wrong type
entries.rationale: A type mismatch can silently change or disable client-specific behavior.

entries.description: Unknown frontmatter field, with vendor-aware suggestions
entries.rationale: Misspelled or unsupported fields create a false expectation that policy is active.

entries.description: Invalid glob syntax
entries.rationale: An invalid pattern cannot define a trustworthy activation set.

entries.description: Empty instruction document
entries.rationale: An empty discovered document adds ambiguity without contributing instructions.

entries.description: Instruction file is stored in a location unsupported by the selected agent
entries.rationale: A recognized document in an unsupported location is unlikely to affect the intended client.

entries.description: Deprecated or legacy instruction format
entries.rationale: Legacy formats can lose support or behave differently from current documented formats.

entries.description: Duplicate frontmatter key
entries.rationale: Duplicate keys have parser-dependent winner semantics and can broaden or narrow scope unexpectedly.

entries.description: Invalid suppression directive
entries.rationale: A malformed directive may fail to suppress the intended finding or conceal reviewer intent.

entries.description: Unused suppression directive
entries.rationale: A stale directive adds policy debt and may unexpectedly match a future finding.

entries.description: Referenced repository file does not exist
entries.rationale: A missing local reference leaves required context unavailable.

entries.description: Import cycle
entries.rationale: Cycles make instruction loading incomplete or client-dependent.

entries.description: Reference escapes repository boundary
entries.rationale: Repository analysis must not claim or read context outside its authorized root.

entries.description: Absolute local path reduces portability
entries.rationale: Machine-specific paths do not transfer reliably across contributors or CI runners.

entries.description: Remote reference is used where the client does not load remote content
entries.rationale: A remote link can look like imported policy even when the selected client never loads it.

entries.description: Reference syntax is unsupported by the target agent
entries.rationale: Unsupported reference syntax cannot supply the intended context.

entries.description: Case mismatch in a path, which can fail on case-sensitive systems
entries.rationale: Case-only path mistakes can pass locally and fail on another supported platform.

entries.description: Scope pattern matches no repository files
entries.rationale: A provably empty scope makes the instruction unreachable.

entries.description: Rule is unintentionally always-on because scope metadata is missing
entries.rationale: Missing scope metadata can add specialized context to every target.

entries.description: Scope is broader than the directory containing the rule suggests
entries.rationale: An unexpectedly broad scope increases conflicts and irrelevant context.

entries.description: Scope is completely shadowed or unreachable
entries.rationale: A fully shadowed rule cannot influence any resolved target.

entries.description: Different agents resolve the same file to materially different scopes
entries.rationale: Cross-client scope divergence undermines a shared repository policy.

entries.description: Nested instruction behavior is ambiguous for a selected client
entries.rationale: Unresolved nesting semantics prevent a definitive effective-context claim.

entries.description: Instruction affects generated, vendored, or dependency files
entries.rationale: Applying repository policy to derived content may waste context or encourage unsafe edits.

entries.description: Mutually exclusive package-manager commands apply to the same target
entries.rationale: Conflicting package-manager requirements cannot both be followed safely.

entries.description: Mutually exclusive required/prohibited action
entries.rationale: The same action cannot be both mandatory and forbidden for one target.

entries.description: Conflicting test, build, formatting, or commit instructions
entries.rationale: Conflicting workflow requirements make successful task completion indeterminate.

entries.description: Near-duplicate instruction appears in multiple effective files
entries.rationale: Repeated effective policy consumes context and increases drift risk.

entries.description: Vendor-specific instruction diverges from canonical `AGENTS.md` policy
entries.rationale: Vendor divergence can produce materially different outcomes across supported agents.

entries.description: A more specific rule repeats an inherited instruction unchanged
entries.rationale: Redundant inherited content adds context without changing effective policy.

entries.description: Referenced script or task does not exist
entries.rationale: An instruction that invokes a missing task cannot be completed as written.

entries.description: Command uses a package manager inconsistent with lockfiles/configuration
entries.rationale: A mismatched package manager can change dependency resolution or corrupt lock state.

entries.description: Mentioned directory, config file, or executable does not exist
entries.rationale: A missing repository resource makes the instruction stale or incomplete.

entries.description: Instruction names a tool absent from project configuration
entries.rationale: An undeclared tool may not exist in clean development or CI environments.

entries.description: Documented runtime version conflicts with repository configuration
entries.rationale: Runtime drift can make documented commands fail or behave differently.

entries.description: Instruction duplicates a policy already enforced mechanically by a linter/formatter
entries.rationale: Mechanically enforced policy need not consume repeated agent context.

entries.description: Always-on context exceeds configured token budget
entries.rationale: Oversized individual documents consume scarce context for every applicable request.

entries.description: Document contains a large code block better referenced from another file
entries.rationale: Duplicated code blocks are costly and can drift from their source.

entries.description: Instruction is vague or not actionable
entries.rationale: Non-actionable prose consumes context without giving an agent a verifiable requirement.

entries.description: Very long instruction combines multiple independent requirements
entries.rationale: Separating independent requirements improves reviewability and targeting.

entries.description: Repository description repeats readily discoverable metadata
entries.rationale: Repeated discoverable facts add context cost without durable policy value.

entries.description: Imported content expands context unexpectedly
entries.rationale: Import amplification can exceed the author-visible size of an instruction document.

entries.description: High-confidence credential or private key appears in an instruction file
entries.rationale: Instruction files are broadly exposed context and must not contain credential material.

entries.description: Instruction requests reading secrets or broad credential locations
entries.rationale: Routine secret access expands the impact of mistakes or prompt injection.

entries.description: Download-and-execute command lacks integrity pinning
entries.rationale: Executing mutable remote bytes prevents reproducible trust decisions.

entries.description: Destructive command is presented as routine or unconditional
entries.rationale: Destructive operations require explicit scope, confirmation, and recovery planning.

entries.description: Instruction disables approvals, sandboxing, or security controls
entries.rationale: Disabling safety controls weakens the repository's intended execution boundary.

entries.description: Instruction requests transmission of repository data to an external destination
entries.rationale: External transmission can disclose source or sensitive repository metadata.

entries.description: Imported instruction source is mutable or unpinned
entries.rationale: Mutable policy can change without repository review or provenance.

entries.description: Policy exists only in a vendor-specific file and has no shared equivalent
entries.rationale: Vendor-only policy leaves other supported agents without the same requirements.

entries.description: Same repository policy differs across agent formats
entries.rationale: Divergent copies make cross-agent outcomes depend on the selected client.

entries.description: Agent does not support the selected import or nesting behavior
entries.rationale: Unsupported composition behavior must be visible rather than assumed effective.

entries.description: Instruction depends on an editor-only feature
entries.rationale: Editor-only behavior does not transfer to headless or hosted agent surfaces.

entries.description: Locked knowledge pack is older than configured maximum age
entries.rationale: An over-age pack may omit reviewed changes in supported specifications.

entries.description: A newer stable knowledge pack is available
entries.rationale: Explicit freshness checks should surface a verified stable update without changing scan state.

entries.description: Knowledge pack requires a newer CLI engine
entries.rationale: An incompatible engine cannot interpret the pack's contracts safely.

entries.description: Knowledge-pack digest or signature validation failed
entries.rationale: Unverified standards data must never influence diagnostics.

entries.description: Repository uses syntax deprecated by the selected specification
entries.rationale: Deprecated syntax can stop working as clients advance.

entries.description: Repository standards lockfile is missing in CI
entries.rationale: Without a lockfile, CI cannot reproduce the standards knowledge used for a scan.

entries.description: Preview upstream behavior exists but is not enabled
entries.rationale: Preview information should be visible without being mistaken for stable active semantics.

entries.description: Always-on context exceeds configured token budget
entries.rationale: Resolved always-on context can exceed a client's usable budget across documents.

entries.description: Effective p95 context exceeds configured token budget
entries.rationale: High-tail effective context can make common targets costly or truncated.

entries.description: High-confidence duplicate context exceeds threshold
entries.rationale: Duplicate effective text spends tokens without adding distinct instruction value.

entries.description: Specialized content appears in an unnecessarily broad scope
entries.rationale: Narrowing specialized content can reduce context while preserving intended targets.

entries.description: Import graph materially amplifies effective context
entries.rationale: Import fan-out can make resolved context much larger than source documents suggest.

entries.description: Vendor-specific duplication can be consolidated safely
entries.rationale: Safe consolidation reduces drift and repeated tokens across agent formats.

entries.description: Instruction density is below configured threshold
entries.rationale: Low-density documents spend context on prose that carries little actionable policy.

entries.description: Efficiency comparison uses incompatible tokenizer versions
entries.rationale: Counts from incompatible tokenizers cannot support a valid comparison.

entries.description: High-impact context reduction is available but not benchmarked
entries.rationale: A projected saving must remain distinct from empirically measured quality preservation.
